meta.title: Fair Harbor: the growth plan
meta.subject: Fair Harbor Clothing PBC (BSP portfolio, entry Mar 2022)
meta.thesis: From DTC swim brand to year-round sustainable lifestyle brand: category extension, wholesale door growth, retention/membership, international; AI agents for fit/size, CX and demand planning; 3PL and returns talent/ops; capital-light financing.
meta.method: Built on 2026-10-06 from the portal's verified datasets (data/research/fairharbor_filings.json, bsp_firm.json bsp-fh item, timeline and Fair Harbor opportunities, rival_filings.json Chubbies items, public_comps.json apparel DTC benchmarks, pe_landscape.json Fair Harbor heatmap, serviceos_evidence.json HarborOS items) plus new web research (search and direct fetches) on vendor claims, analog brands, returns/3PL benchmarks and lending norms. data/research/pp_nationwide.json was not present, so item shape follows ServiceOS evidence conventions (kind, id, source URL, retrieved, est. labels). Computed data points (markdown share, non-swim share, Chubbies channel mix and growth, B2B SKU count, ABL capacity, leverage capacity) are calculated in the build script from those datasets; the KPI roadmap and all targets are explicit analyst assumptions anchored to the filings estimate table.
caveats: Fair Harbor has never disclosed revenue, EBITDA or debt; the $27M revenue and 6% EBITDA baseline are midpoints of low-confidence estimates ($20-35M; 0-12%).
Vendor metrics (Bold Metrics, Gorgias, Loop, Global-e, Meta, ShipBob, Happy Returns, Metyis) are self-reported, self-selected and unaudited; treat them as upper bounds.
The McKinsey forecasting figure (20-50% fewer errors, up to 65% fewer lost sales) was confirmed via HubSpot's citation of the McKinsey article; the McKinsey page itself timed out on direct fetch.
Faherty's ~$250M figure comes from a Guy Raz newsletter describing it as a '$250 million lifestyle brand'; it is not an audited revenue number.
Door counts date from the 2022 release (~250 specialty plus Nordstrom and Saks); the current stockist list is not public, so the door baseline may be stale.
Weeks-to-deploy, ABL inputs (58% gross margin, 2.5x turns, 40% wholesale, 45-day DSO) and every KPI target are analyst assumptions labelled est.
Middle-market leverage (3.8x) is an all-sector figure; no consumer-apparel-specific LMM leverage figure was verified.
The current lender after the Dec 2025 eCapital lien release is unknown.
Smith + Howard is used only as a template (exited Aug 2026); it is not an active company.
narrative: About 4.5 years in, Fair Harbor, BSP's only consumer brand, is still a ~$27M business (est. range $20-35M) with low single-digit EBITDA and no add-ons.
The shift to a year-round lifestyle brand has already happened on the shelf: 64.0% of the 372 live products are non-swim, and golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom launched in 2025-2026.
Margin is the problem: 38.5% of live variants are marked down, women's was cleared at ~70% off, and swim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands (21.6%).
So the first six months are about fixing the base (markdown discipline, fit and returns, and buying to forecast) before we pay for growth.
Chubbies is the proof case for the next step: at $122.9M it takes 51.9% of sales from wholesale and retail, that channel grew 16.3% last year, and its DTC fell 20.8% in Q2 2026.
Our plan is to take Fair Harbor from ~250 specialty doors to ~520 over 36 months through golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty, using commissioned reps rather than new owned stores.
Retention is the cheapest growth: repeat-purchase benchmarks are 20-30%, and Klaviyo flows earn about 41% of email revenue from 5% of sends.

HarborOS, at an est. $0.3-0.7M, puts nine agents on that work (fit, CX, returns-to-exchange, demand planning, markdowns, lifecycle, paid media, cross-border and wholesale reorders); vendor claims include 60% ticket automation and 17% fewer fit returns.
International starts in month 30 as merchant-of-record DTC into Canada, the UK and Australia, following Vuori's e-commerce-first launch, because the store ships only to the US today.
We should stay capital-light: the unsold ~$6M of the 2022 equity sleeve and an ABL of roughly $3.4-4.6M cover the plan, and Solo Brands' delisting shows what term debt does to a swim brand.

The roadmap assumes revenue grows from ~$27M to ~$40M and EBITDA from ~$1.6M to ~$5.2M by month 36. That is still below Chubbies' 18% margin, and every figure is an analyst assumption, not company data.

The Smith + Howard lesson applies: buyers paid for a scaled, legible portfolio company, so the exit story is wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, and the logical buyers are strategics and brand owners.

kpi_roadmap.note: Baseline = Fair Harbor filings estimate table point (2025 net revenue ~$27M, range $20-35M; EBITDA 0-12%, midpoint 6%); headcount 40-80 midpoint; ~250 specialty doors + Nordstrom + Saks (2022 release) + 2 owned stores. All low confidence.

items.move: Entry: founder-led regional leader, first institutional capital
items.what_they_did: BSP made a strategic anchor investment in Smith + Howard (Atlanta, ~100 professionals, one office) in Nov 2022.
items.fair_harbor_translation: Fair Harbor is the same set-up in consumer: a founder-led brand taking its first institutional capital ($30.7M Form D, Mar 2022). The S+H lesson is that the entry thesis named the adjacent services up front; Fair Harbor's equivalent is a named category-and-channel map (year-round apparel, golf, collegiate, B2B, international).

items.move: First adjacent-market step: merge with a like-minded firm next door
items.what_they_did: Merged with Market Street Partners (Chattanooga) in Aug 2023, its first move beyond Atlanta.
items.fair_harbor_translation: For Fair Harbor the 'next city' is the next door type: green-grass golf pro shops via FootJoy (18 collab SKUs) and sporting-goods doors like Scheels, before any new owned store.

items.move: Capability add-ons that widen the menu sold to existing clients
items.what_they_did: Added benefit-plan audit (JMM CPAs, Chicago, Jan 2024) and executive search (VIP Search/VIP Solutions, Dallas, Apr 2024).
items.fair_harbor_translation: Category extension is Fair Harbor's version: 372 live products, 64.0% of them non-swim, plus kids (51) and B2B custom (88 SKUs). Every new category should be sold first to the existing customer file and the existing door list.

items.move: Density in a chosen region, deal after deal
items.what_they_did: Fahrenheit Advisors (Richmond, Dec 2024), Smith Kesler (Carolinas, Jan 2025), Horton Lee & Burnett (Birmingham, Sep 2025), Bauknight Pietras & Stormer (SC, Jan 2026).
items.fair_harbor_translation: Fair Harbor should build door density in its proven coastal and golf geographies (Northeast, Florida, the Carolinas) before spreading thin, so reps, trunk shows and co-op marketing are shared across doors.

items.move: Technology, AI and offshore delivery as the margin engine
items.what_they_did: Per the exit release, BSP invested in leadership, technology, AI-enabled capabilities and an offshore delivery centre in India; Geels Norton (cyber, Feb 2026) added a tech-heavy service line.
items.fair_harbor_translation: HarborOS is the consumer equivalent: fit/size, CX, returns-to-exchange and demand-planning agents on Shopify/Klaviyo, sized at $0.3-0.7M for 2-5 points of EBITDA margin (ServiceOS evidence ra-fh, est.).

items.move: The exit: a scaled, buyer-legible portfolio company sold to a growth investor
items.what_they_did: Sold to TPG (TPG Growth), closed Aug 6 2026 after ~3.5 years: ~100 to ~800 professionals, 1 to 11 Southeast locations plus India, 9 add-ons, nearly 4x revenue.
items.fair_harbor_translation: Fair Harbor is ~4.5 years into its hold with no add-ons (FH-16). The S+H template says the exit story must be a scaled company with visible recurring earnings; for a brand that means wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, not just top-line.

items.move: Vertical analog 1: men's swim/lifestyle brand that grew through wholesale
items.what_they_did: Chubbies reached $122.9M FY2025 sales with 51.9% from retail and wholesale (that channel +16.3% vs DTC +2.3%), a 18.2% segment EBITDA margin and 11 stores; Solo Brands paid $129.5M in Sept 2021 funded by a $100M term loan. In Q2 2026 its DTC fell 20.8% while wholesale held.
items.fair_harbor_translation: This is the clearest proof that wholesale breadth, not DTC alone, carries a men's swim brand past $100M; and that a leveraged owner (Solo was delisted in July 2026 with ~$249M debt) can damage a good brand. It is also a possible add-on or door-share opportunity if Chubbies is sold.

items.move: Vertical analog 2: DTC apparel brand that went omnichannel and international
items.what_they_did: Vuori sold through Nordstrom and REI, raised $400M at a $4B valuation (SoftBank, Oct 2021) to fund ~100 US stores, and in Mar 2022 launched e-commerce in the UK, France, Germany, Ireland, Netherlands, Australia and Canada with wholesale partners (Selfridges, Cotswold Outdoor, Bever) and a UK distribution hub.
items.fair_harbor_translation: International should start as localized DTC in English-speaking coastal markets with a merchant-of-record partner and a few premium wholesale partners, as Vuori did, not with owned stores.

items.move: Vertical analog 3: beach-born lifestyle brand built on all three channels
items.what_they_did: Faherty (founded 2013, beach-inspired) launched DTC, wholesale and retail almost at once and reached a ~$250M lifestyle brand with nearly 80 stores; Bloomberg reported in Nov 2023 that the family explored selling a minority stake.
items.fair_harbor_translation: The closest positioning analog to Fair Harbor (coastal, year-round lifestyle). It shows the ceiling of the category, but its store-heavy route is capital-intensive; Fair Harbor should borrow the specialty-door relationships and year-round assortment, not the 80-store fleet.

items.name: Fix the base: markdowns, returns and inventory
geography: United States DTC (97.2% of web traffic is US)
Owned stores: SoHo NYC, Palm Beach Gardens FL
items.thesis: Margin before growth. 38.5% of live variants carried markdowns in Sept 2026 and the women's line was cleared at ~70% off; swim returns run ~21.6% at Shopify brands. Fix price, fit and buys before spending on doors.

items.name: International DTC and exit readiness
items.thesis: Open cross-border DTC where coastal lifestyle sells, through a merchant-of-record partner, then take a wholesale-heavy, margin-positive brand to market. Today the store ships only to the US. Exit buyers will be strategics and brand owners; Chubbies sold at ~$129.5M and Fair Harbor's entry EV was an estimated $40-90M.

items.description: $30.7M of primary equity sold to 24 investors on 2022-03-15, $6.0M of $36.7M authorized still unsold; about 9.2% of Fund I's $335M. No proceeds to officers.
items.implication: The unsold ~$6.0M sleeve is the natural source for the $0.3-0.7M HarborOS build and any small brand tuck-in; no new sponsor cheque is needed for the plan.

items.instrument: Asset-based revolver history and likely refinancing
items.description: USPTO records show ABL security interests on the core mark from Merchant Financial (2020-2021) and Gerber Finance/eCapital (2021, released 2025-12-11); the core marks were assigned to Fair Harbor Clothing Topco LLC the same day.

key_figures.ip_holdco: Fair Harbor Clothing Topco LLC (Jersey City)

items.implication: Same-day lien release and IP move to a Topco usually mean a new lender or a restructured collateral package. Diligence should confirm the current facility, covenants and whether store leases sit inside the borrowing base.

items.description: Lenders typically advance 50-75% against inventory and 85-90% against receivables (U.S. Bank).

key_figures.assumptions: est.: revenue $27M, gross margin 58% (Chubbies FY2025 57.9%), 2.5x inventory turns, 40% wholesale, 45-day DSO

items.implication: An ABL sized to Fair Harbor's working capital is roughly $3.4-4.6M (est.), enough to fund the seasonal swim build and wholesale receivables without term debt.

items.description: Middle-market debt/EBITDA averaged 3.8x year-to-date Q3 2025, down from 4.0x in H1 2025 (Mercer Capital).
items.implication: At est. EBITDA of ~$1.6M today the market norm implies only ~$6M of term debt, and a cyclical, weather-exposed brand should run well below the norm. Recommendation: stay capital-light (ABL only) until EBITDA clears ~$4-5M.

items.instrument: Cautionary precedent: leveraged owner of the closest rival
items.description: Solo Brands funded the $129.5M Chubbies purchase with a $100M term loan (Sept 2021); Solo was removed from the NYSE in July 2026 carrying ~$249M of long-term debt.
items.implication: Debt, not the brand, is what broke the Chubbies owner. It also creates an opening: Chubbies or its doors could come loose, and Fair Harbor's light balance sheet makes it a credible buyer or partner.

items.description: COVID EIDL of $150,000 (30-year direct loan) taken May 2020; PPP of $16,994 in Apr 2020.
items.implication: Immaterial today; payoff status not public. Confirm it was repaid at the 2022 close.
